name: Srinagar
tagline: The Venice of the East & Heart of the Valley
description: Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu & Kashmir, is world-famous for its tranquil Dal and Nigeen Lakes, floating vegetable gardens, hand-carved cedar houseboats, and Mughal terraced gardens built by emperors who called it paradise on earth.
best_time_to_visit: April to October (Pleasant greenery) & Dec to Feb (Snow lovers)
how_to_reach: Fly directly into Sheikh ul-Alam International Airport (SXR), located just 12 km from Srinagar city center.

name: Gulmarg
tagline: Meadow of Flowers & Asia's Premier Ski Paradise
description: Perched at 8,690 ft, Gulmarg is an alpine wonderland boasting the world's second highest operating cable car (the Gulmarg Gondola), powdery ski slopes in winter, and rolling green golf courses and wildflower meadows in summer.
best_time_to_visit: Dec to March for deep powder snow & skiing; May to Sept for verdant green meadows.
how_to_reach: 51 km (approx. 1.5 - 2 hrs) scenic mountain drive from Srinagar Airport.

name: Pahalgam
tagline: Valley of Shepherds & Confluence of Lidder Streams
description: Surrounded by soaring pine forests, glacial streams, and snow-crowned peaks, Pahalgam is the serene gateway to the Amarnath Yatra and home to the world-renowned Betaab and Aru Valleys.
best_time_to_visit: March to November for lush scenery and Lidder riverside stays.
how_to_reach: 95 km (approx. 2.5 hrs) drive from Srinagar via the fragrant saffron fields of Pampore.

name: Sonamarg
tagline: The Meadow of Gold & Gateway to Ladakh
description: Nestled in the Sindh Valley at 9,000 ft, Sonamarg is framed by majestic glaciers, roaring mountain rivers, and alpine flower pastures. It serves as the base for Thajiwas Glacier and the Baltal Amarnath route.
best_time_to_visit: April to October (Accessible via Srinagar-Leh highway).
how_to_reach: 80 km (approx. 2 hrs) scenic drive from Srinagar following the gushing Sindh River.

name: Doodhpathri
tagline: Valley of Milk & Untouched Green Slopes
description: A tranquil eco-paradise in Budgam district where the roaring Shaliganga river foams like pure white milk over pebbles. Surrounded by dense deodar forests, it remains blessedly calm and pristine.
best_time_to_visit: May to October for green velvet meadows.
how_to_reach: 42 km (approx. 1.5 hrs) picturesque drive from Srinagar.

name: Gurez Valley
tagline: The Crown of Kashmir & Land of Habba Khatoon
description: Secluded beyond the 11,672 ft Razdan Pass, Gurez is a breathtaking remote valley where the turquoise Kishanganga River flows beside the triangular Habba Khatoon peak. The people speak the Dardic-Shina tongue and offer authentic mountain warmth.
best_time_to_visit: June to September when Razdan Pass is snow-free.
how_to_reach: 125 km (approx. 5-6 hrs) scenic drive from Srinagar via Bandipora and Razdan Pass.

name: Bungus Valley
tagline: The Hidden Highland Wilderness of Kupwara
description: Spanning over 300 square kilometers of virgin alpine pastures, Bungus is divided into Bod Bungus (Greater Bungus) and Lokut Bungus (Lesser Bungus). It is an untouched haven of wild flora and fauna.
best_time_to_visit: June to September.
how_to_reach: 115 km from Srinagar via Handwara / Kupwara, followed by a light trek or 4x4 trail.

name: Drung Waterfall
tagline: The Frozen Winter Cascade of Tangmarg
description: Located near Tangmarg on the way to Gulmarg, Drung features a roaring waterfall that completely freezes into majestic ice pillars during peak winter, creating an otherworldly icy fairytale.
best_time_to_visit: December to February for the frozen waterfall; May to August for lush greenery.
how_to_reach: 42 km from Srinagar, 10 minutes diversion from Tangmarg town.

name: Verinag
tagline: The Origin of River Jhelum & Mughal Octagonal Spring
description: Situated at the foothills of the Pir Panjal range, Verinag is where the life-giving Jhelum River emerges from a deep turquoise spring. Emperor Jahangir constructed an octagonal stone basin and lush garden around it in 1620 AD.
best_time_to_visit: April to October.
how_to_reach: 78 km south of Srinagar via the Jammu-Srinagar Highway.

name: Aru Valley
tagline: Scenic High Meadow & Base for Kolahoi Glacier
description: Just 12 km upstream from Pahalgam, Aru is a peaceful postcard village nestled beside gurgling streams and pine woods. It serves as the primary base camp for treks to Kolahoi Glacier and Tarsar Marsar lakes.
best_time_to_visit: May to October for trekking; Dec to Feb for peaceful winter snow.
how_to_reach: 12 km drive from Pahalgam taxi stand.

name: Aharbal Waterfall
tagline: The Niagara Falls of Kashmir
description: In Kulgam district, the roaring Veshav River crashes down a 25-meter sheer basalt cliff in a cloud of spray. Aharbal is beloved for its dramatic volume of water and pine-forested river canyon.
best_time_to_visit: April to October.
how_to_reach: 70 km from Srinagar via Shopian apple orchards.

name: Leh
tagline: The High Altitude Desert Capital & Tibetan Citadel
description: Set amidst dramatic brown barren mountains at 11,500 ft, Leh is the spiritual and cultural heart of Ladakh, rich with 17th-century palaces, whitewashed stupas, and ancient Buddhist gompas.
best_time_to_visit: May to September for clear skies and warm days.
how_to_reach: Fly to Leh Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport (IXL) or overland drive via Srinagar-Leh highway.

name: Nubra Valley
tagline: Valley of Flowers, Cold Deserts & Double-Humped Camels
description: Located north of Leh across the mighty Khardung La, Nubra Valley features an extraordinary contrast of towering snowy peaks and white sand dunes where rare Bactrian double-humped camels roam.
best_time_to_visit: May to October.
how_to_reach: 150 km from Leh via Khardung La Pass (approx. 5 hrs).
top_activities: Luxury Swiss glamping under star-filled skies

name: Pangong Lake
tagline: The High Altitude Color-Changing Enchanted Lake
description: Spanning 134 km across India and Tibet at 14,270 ft, Pangong Tso is legendary for its mesmerizing color shifts from turquoise blue to deep indigo. The crystal reflections of jagged brown mountains are unforgettable.
best_time_to_visit: May to September.
how_to_reach: 160 km from Leh via Chang La pass, or direct via Shyok river route from Nubra.

name: Khardung La
tagline: The Legend of 17,982 ft — Conquering the High Pass
description: One of the highest motorable mountain passes on Earth, Khardung La provides panoramic vistas of the Karakoram range to the north and the Ladakh range to the south.
best_time_to_visit: May to October.
how_to_reach: 39 km uphill drive from Leh town.

name: Tso Moriri
tagline: The Sacred High Wetland & Changpa Nomad Sanctuary
description: Perched at 14,836 ft in the remote Changthang region, Tso Moriri is a pristine, tranquil blue high-altitude wetland sanctuary hosting rare bar-headed geese and wild Tibetan asses (Kiang).
best_time_to_visit: June to September.
how_to_reach: 220 km southeast of Leh via Chumathang hot springs.

name: Sham Valley
tagline: The Apricot Valley & Cultural Heart of Lower Ladakh
description: Known as the Apricot Blossom route, Sham Valley encompasses the dramatic confluence of the Indus and Zanskar rivers, the gravity-defying Magnetic Hill, and the 1,000-year-old Alchi Monastery.
best_time_to_visit: April for Apricot flowers; May to October for sightseeing.
how_to_reach: West of Leh along the Leh-Kargil National Highway (30 to 70 km).

name: Jammu
tagline: The City of Temples & Gateway to the Shrines
description: Situated on the banks of Tawi River, Jammu is renowned for its grand historic temples, the ornate Bahu Fort, and the opulent Mubarak Mandi Palace, serving as the transportation gateway to Kashmir and Katra.
best_time_to_visit: September to April for pleasant weather.
how_to_reach: Major railway terminal (Jammu Tawi - JAT) and domestic airport (IXJ).
top_activities: Tasting traditional Kalari cheese & Rajma Chawal

name: Katra
tagline: The Sacred Base Camp for Mata Vaishno Devi
description: Lying at the foot of the Trikuta Mountains, Katra is a bustling holy town tailored for millions of pilgrims visiting Mata Vaishno Devi. It features excellent hotels, pure vegetarian dining, and helicopter services.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round pilgrimage; March to October is especially popular.
how_to_reach: 48 km from Jammu via highway, or directly by train at Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra railway station (SVDK).
top_attractions: Katra Market for Walnuts & Dry Fruits

name: Vaishno Devi
tagline: The Holy Cave Shrine of Mata Rani in Trikuta Hills
description: One of India's most venerated Hindu shrines, the Holy Cave of Mata Vaishno Devi sits at 5,200 ft. Millions of devotees chant 'Jai Mata Di' during the 12 km trek from Katra to attain blessings from the holy Pindies.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round; Navratri festivals in April and October are deeply festive.
how_to_reach: 12 km paved uphill track or 8-minute helicopter flight from Katra to Sanjichhat.
top_attractions: Bhairon Baba Temple via Cable Car
